_comment: The pre-filter questions. `label` is what the clinician reads; `facet` is
what the model judges each passage against, so the two are tuned
independently — a label can be short where a facet has to be explicit.
Facets are written to DISCRIMINATE. A facet that could describe half the
library ("clinical care") makes its answer useless as a filter, and the
recall-biased prompt will attach it to nearly everything. Name the
vocabulary a relevant passage would actually contain.
Editing this file invalidates every stored judgement automatically — the
cache key hashes the content, so no version bump is required (though
bumping `version` is still good manners for a deliberate redesign).

questions.help_text: The clinical area. Pick more than one if the question spans them.

answers.label: Infection & antimicrobials
answers.facet: infection, antibiotics, antimicrobial choice or duration, cultures, sepsis, resistant organisms, isolation and infection-control precautions

answers.label: Cardiac & vascular
answers.facet: chest pain, acute coronary syndrome, ECG changes, cardiac biomarkers, reperfusion, antithrombotic therapy, blood pressure and cardiovascular risk

answers.label: Metabolic & endocrine
answers.facet: diabetes, glycaemic targets, insulin and oral hypoglycaemics, HbA1c, and metabolic or endocrine complications

answers.label: Sedation, analgesia & delirium
answers.facet: sedation depth and agents, analgesia and opioids, delirium screening or treatment, and neuromuscular blockade

questions.help_text: Where care is being delivered — this changes the regimen more than anything else.

answers.label: Intensive care
answers.facet: critical care: mechanically ventilated, haemodynamically unstable or organ-supported patients, ICU protocols and infusions

answers.label: Hospital ward
answers.facet: inpatient care outside intensive care: hospital admission criteria, inpatient regimens, intravenous therapy on a general ward, and discharge planning

answers.label: Outpatient / community
answers.facet: management outside hospital: primary care, clinic and community treatment, oral outpatient regimens, and routine follow-up between visits

answers.label: Theatre / periprocedural
answers.facet: operating theatre, anaesthesia, surgical prophylaxis, and immediate pre- or post-operative management

questions.prompt: What do you need to decide?
questions.help_text: Where you are in the decision — the same topic reads very differently at each stage.

answers.label: Diagnose or assess
answers.facet: reaching a diagnosis: presentation, examination, investigations, laboratory or imaging tests, diagnostic criteria, severity scores and risk stratification

answers.label: Choose treatment
answers.facet: choosing and giving treatment: drug selection, dose, route, regimen, escalation or de-escalation, procedures and interventions

answers.label: Monitor or follow up
answers.facet: what happens after treatment starts: monitoring parameters, targets and reassessment, adverse effects, complications, safety and long-term follow-up

questions.help_text: Optional. Leave blank unless the patient's group changes the answer.

answers.label: Pregnancy
answers.facet: pregnancy, obstetric, peripartum or breastfeeding patients, including drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

answers.label: Children
answers.facet: paediatric, neonatal or adolescent patients, including weight-based paediatric dosing

answers.label: Renal or hepatic impairment
answers.facet: chronic kidney disease, renal or hepatic impairment, dose adjustment for organ dysfunction, and nephrotoxicity

answers.label: Elderly / frail
answers.facet: elderly or frail patients, polypharmacy, falls and age-adjusted targets or thresholds
